lead: Jackson plumbing deals with shifting Yazoo clay, aging city water lines, heat and the occasional hard freeze. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Jackson.
risk: broken lines from shifting clay, boil-water notices and frozen pipes
risk_short: clay soil, water outages and frozen pipes
why: Much of Jackson sits on Yazoo clay, which swells and shrinks a great deal. That movement cracks slabs, sewer laterals and water lines. Belhaven, Fondren and Eastover have homes from the 1920s to the 1950s with galvanized lines.
The city's water system has struggled, with boil-water notices and the 2022 plant failure. Hard freezes, like 2021 and 2022, burst many exposed pipes.
water: Jackson's water system is run by JXN Water under a federal court arrangement. It treats water from the Ross Barnett Reservoir and the Pearl River. Watch for boil-water notices.
tips: Sign up for JXN Water alerts.
Keep bottled water on hand for boil-water notices.
Insulate exposed pipes before a freeze.
Water your foundation evenly in dry spells.
areas: PipeMend works in Belhaven, Fondren, Eastover, Downtown, North Jackson, South Jackson, LeFleur East and every other Jackson neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Jackson Planning and Development Department. Mississippi's State Board of Contractors licenses larger plumbing contracts, and the city may also require a local license.

faq.a: Yazoo clay is a very expansive soil found under much of the Jackson area. It swells when wet and shrinks when dry, which cracks foundations, sewer lines and water lines.
